newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: UBS HAS WORDING OBSTACLES IN LIT-TEL DEAL.
newsitem.headline: UBS HAS WORDING OBSTACLES IN LIT-TEL DEAL.

text.p: Translation glitches are the only obstacles to Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) becoming the government's adviser in the Lithuanian Telecom privatisation, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday.

"In essence the government approved the draft agreement but there are some minor editorial details," Vagnorius told Reuters. "If the company refuses to introduce the changes...the government will have to make a different decision."
Vagnorius said the English and Lithuanian texts of the agreement did not match because some terms in the English version of the agreement did not exist in Lithuanian legislation.
"According to the agreement, all arguments or disputes are settled according to Lithuanian law," Vagnorius said.
Vagnorius said the agreement with UBS could be signed soon.
"It all depends on UBS," Vagnorius said.
Lithuanian Telecom is one of over a dozen key state-owned enterprises the government is privatising this year and in 1998 by open international tender.

UBS was announced the winner of the tender earlier this month after becoming one of seven candidates to make the short list of applicants to be the government's lead adviser in the Telecom privatisation.
The European Affairs Ministry said then that Deutche Morgan Grenfell was the runner-up in the tender and would be the government's second choice if an agreement with UBS could not be reached.
